description: We are a team participating in NASA Space Apps 2026 from Denizli Anatolian Imam Hatip High School in Türkiye. With our project VITA-NET, we are building a real-time health monitoring system for astronauts. In deep space, delayed medical alerts put lives at risk. Our ultra-fast platform tracks telemetry and evaluates health risks to protect crews. Join our mission to make space safer!
summary: VITA-NET TECH, is a health monitoring and support platform designed to support well-being of astronauts during long space missions, and it uses an artificial intelligence chatbot including multilingual accessibility. The system tracks physiological indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature and cumulative radiation exposure. The platform combines real-time health assessment, automated risk detection, AI assisted recommendations and multilingual accessibility. Thus, it helps space crews monitor potential medical risks before they become life threatening emergencies.
details:
What is the project used for?

VITA-NET TECH, collects and interprets astronauts’ health data continuously, every four seconds. The system compares the data with internationally recognised health criteria, obtained from World Health Organisation and NASA radiation exposure standards. It categorizes measured data as “OK”, “Watch”, “Critical” according to risk rates. So, astronauts or healthcare workers can recognize possible health risks immediately.

 

The platform displays mission status, real-time location data of International Space Station (ISS), health trends, simulated extravehicular activity (EVA), oxygen levels and emergency scenarios in addition to physiological monitoring; all on a single control panel. The interface offers multi language support in 16 languages to improve usability in different task environments and with astronauts from different countries. 

 

How does the system work?

The platform has a layered client-server architecture.  Health measurements obtained from sensors are transmitted to a Python-based backend, where they are verified and analyzed. The backend compares incoming data to universally recognised health thresholds and transmits the received information to the user interface via WebSocket. Thus, it provides real-time information without requiring page refreshes.

 

Our project consists of four main steps;

First, health and mission data is collected and verified using Pydantic diagram. Data is processed simultaneously. The backend analyzes vital signs and radiation exposure levels based on mission conditions, and issues alerts when necessary.

 

When a problem occurs, AI models in the system provide guidance by making logical and quick decisions based on the situation. If the connection is lost and these services can not be accessed, the locally based system makes suggestions according to its own logic and enables managing the situation without problems. 

 

Benefits of the project:

- The system enables early detection of the potential health and well being problems in space missions and warns for precautions before danger.

- Given the communication delays that occur during deep space exploration, it is an advantage for astronauts to be able to address their own medical needs

- It determines how to predict radiation exposure risks in advance 

- It ensures ease of use for crews from different countries by offering various language options, even during internet outages or when AI services are down
 

Intended effect:

During long-duration missions to the Moon and beyond, astronauts are exposed to factors such as radiation, microgravity, isolation, and communication delays. This project offers practical solutions by directly analyzing the health data of crew members. It aims to reduce reliance on Earth-based support; it supports the project crew in enhancing and safety, preventing mission durations from being extended due to health reasons, and ensuring uninterrupted mission continuity, and aims to contribute to future space technologies.

 

In addition to space exploration, this architecture can also be effectively utilized in telemedicine settings, disaster response operations, polar research stations, military deployments, and other regions where immediate access to healthcare professionals is limited.

Technologies Used:
- Python 3
- JavaScript (ES6 Modules)
- HTML5
- CSS3
- SQL (SQLite database)

Software Framework and Libraries:
- FastAPI
- Uvicorn
- WebSockets
- Pydantic
- Pytest
- Python-Dotenv

AI tools

The platform draws on multiple AI sources to generate context-appropriate recommendations and maintain control during emergencies:


- NVIDIA NIM 

- Anthropic Claude

- Google Gemini

- OpenRouter

- Local Rule Engine

Database and storage:
History, vital signs, alerts and task conditions for the local SQLite database

Developments and Testing Tools:
- Automated testing framework Pytest
- Schema validation through Pydantic
- Python-Dotevn through management of environmental conditions

Creativity and innovative aspect of the project 

Rather than examining the data of all astronauts together in a collective setting, analyzing each person’s data individually allows more rapid detection of details that might otherwise be overlooked. For potential problems in communication or loss of connections, the system provides rapid guidance through an AI powered model. Instead of a single standard language, it provides 16 languages, multilingual accessibility for astronauts from different nations.

Key Factors to Consider During Development 

The team has addressed some of the critical challenges associated with human space flight when the team designs solution:

- Communication Delays: Significant delays may be experienced in the communication between medical teams on Earth and astronauts on deep space missions. Therefore, the platform  prioritizes decision  support on the vehicle.
-The safety of the crew: The system continuously monitors the health risks and alerts before emergency situations occur.

Reliability:
Local rule engine, AI and external models support missions to continue uninterrupted when there are connection problems.

Accessibility:
Multi-language support, increase ease of use for crew members from different countries.

Data Integrity:
To ensure the system’s robustness, schema validation, automated tests, and secure configuration management have been implemented

Open Science and transparency:
The project adopts the principles of open source developments and uses open standards and sets accessible to everyone as much as possible.


NASA and Space Related Data Sources

The project utilizes NASA standards and space related data sources:

- NASA Space Flight Human-System Standard (NASA-STD-3001)

- Radiation exposure limits and astronaut health standards.

- NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer (OCHMO)

- Health guidelines for human spaceflight.

- Real-Time International Space Station (ISS) Location Tracking

- Monitoring the ISS’s current location.

- World Health Organization (WHO) Guidelines

- Reference ranges for vital signs.

- National council on Radiation Protection and Measurements (NCRP)

- Occupational radiation exposure limits.


References:
- Human Spaceflight Standards
- International Space Station Current Location
- Hypertension

Conclusion:

This project is an AI powered health monitoring and decision-support platform developed to protect crew health during future lunar and deep-space missions. One of the major healthcare challenges of deep-space exploration is the difficulty of responding effectively to medical emergencies when communication with earth is delayed or unavailable. The platform addresses this challenge by integrating real time physiological monitoring, radiation tracking, intelligent alerts, multilingual support, and an autonomous decision-making mechanism into a single system. 

By continuously monitoring critical physiological indicators, the platform performs real-time health assessments and risk analysis. This helps identify potential health issues and emergency situations that could threaten crew safety before they escalate into critical treats. In addition, displaying all relevant time and enabling faster access to essential health information.

Thanks to its built-in rule-based intelligence, the platform remains operational even during network interruptions, ensuring continuous health monitoring and keeping the crew quickly informed of any developments. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, this project offers a practical, measurable, and innovative approach to improving crew health and mission success by addressing communication challenges and medical limitations in deep-space missions.
